title: Resumable weight snapshots and KV consistency playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic spec for resumable weight snapshotting, mmap resume semantics, and tight KV-cache / model-weight consistency. It is intended to be an engineering playbook (not a final API) that teams can reference for implementation and SRE runbooks. The goal is to enable incremental startup (fast resume), safe hot-replace, and predictable KV-cache semantics across rolling rollouts and failure/restart scenarios.

Context and motivation:
- Customers run large models where full weight loads are expensive in memory/time. We need resume-friendly loading to reduce downtime and reduce tail latency when pods restart or get preempted.
- mmap-backed weight storage + safetensors fallback is already in use; we need clear semantics for partially applied patches and atomic commits so a restarted process never sees a half-applied model state.
- KV cache (attention caches) must be versioned alongside weight snapshots to avoid serving responses computed against mismatched parameters.

Design goals (non-functional):
- Atomicity: snapshot activation should be atomic from the serving layer POV; either new weights+kv-version are active, or old ones remain.
- Resumability: worker process should resume load from a checkpoint without re-downloading entire artifacts where possible.
- Integrity: strong checks (sha256) before activation, with a fallback path to known-good artifacts.
- Opacity to user: rollout/canary logic handles compatibility; models pinned by config continue to operate.
- Minimal memory churn: support streaming activation that avoids full second copy in RAM wherever possible.

Key concepts and primitives:
- Snapshot manifest (manifest.json): small JSON describing a weight snapshot. Fields: snapshot_id, model_version, segment_list (ordered), segment_metadata (offset, length, sha256), mmap_hint (hot/cold), kv_generation_id, activation_mode (strict|compat|defer), commit_token (UUID).
- Segment: a contiguous file chunk (safetensors or raw shard). Segments are the unit of incremental fetch and validation.
- Activation plan: ordered list of actions (prepare segments, validate, pin kernel variants, swap metadata pointer).
- Atomic activation token: a two-phase commit token written to local control-plane store (on-disk small file) that indicates intent and final commit.

Loading flow (happy path):
1) Controller downloads manifest only (very small).
2) Controller evaluates activation_mode and resource constraints.
3) For each segment flagged hot in mmap_hint: start parallel mmap open + async read of header and sha256 stream. Cold segments are lazily mapped later.
4) Write a local temp area: /var/lib/rw/runtime/snapshots/<snapshot_id>/segments/<segment>.part while validating sha256. Keep an entry in local load-state: {segment, offset, validated_bytes}.
5) Once all hot segments validated, create activation_token status=prepared and fsync token file.
6) Atomically swap model pointer: replace active_snapshot symlink with new snapshot directory (atomic rename). Activation_token updated to committed with timestamp and kv_generation_id.
7) Background: continue streaming remaining cold segments into the snapshot store; those can be activated lazily on first use.

Notes about mmap resume and zero-copy goals:
- For large read-only segments, prefer MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_POPULATE where kernel supports it. If kernel/driver constraints prevent MAP_POPULATE, use small async prefetch windows to warm pages.
- To avoid double-copy during activation, the active symlink points to the directory with pages that were validated in place (we validate by creating .part and renaming). The rename ensures readers either see old or new directory.
- If we must transform tensors (float->quantized), do transformation into a separate storage area and mark those segments as derived in manifest. Derived segments carry origin_sha256 and derived_sha256.

KV-cache versioning and consistency:
- KV generation id (kv_generation_id) is emitted by the model toolchain when a snapshot is produced. Any KV-cache entries must carry kv_generation_id. During activation the runtime checks active_snapshot.kv_generation_id vs current_kv_root. If mismatch, there are three options based on activation_mode:
  - strict: drop all KV cache on activation and start cold (safe).
  - compat: keep KV entries where dtype/size match and reconstruct a compatibility layer for small differences.
  - defer: continue serving old snapshot until operator explicitly promotes new snapshot.
- To implement drops efficiently: use generation bitmaps (per-core bitmap) so invalidation can be O(1) for writers and lazily freed by background GC.
- For multi-model routing: kv entries must be namespaced by snapshot_id to avoid cross-pollination.

Failure modes and recovery:
- If a process crashes while token status=prepared: on restart, check token; if segments validated exist, perform a fast commit by renaming symlink and marking token committed. If validation incomplete, resume fetching remaining segments.
- Corrupt segment detection: if sha256 mismatch, attempt up to N alternate mirrors, then mark snapshot as bad and roll back to previous active snapshot. Emit alert and increment rollback counter metric (runtime.snapshot.rollback.count).
- Half-activated mmap pages: rely on atomic symlink swap to prevent. Readers should open via resolved path to avoid race on symlink changes during open; to be safe, we use O_CLOEXEC + openat semantics in the runtime.

Hot-replace / rollback protocol (operator playbook):
- Canary rollout: create snapshot, set activation_mode=defer on 10% of pods (randomized), observe error/latency delta with test prompts. If healthy, promote to compat then strict.
- Quick rollback: activation_token provides previous_snapshot ref. On operator rollback request, write rollback intent and atomically swap symlink back to previous_snapshot. Background GC will retire new snapshot after grace period.

Operational signals to expose:
- snapshot.load.latency histogram
- snapshot.validate.bytes_total
- snapshot.activation.duration
- snapshot.rollback.count
- kv.generation.mismatch.rate
- snapshot.corruption.retries
These drive dashboards and automated canary promotions.

Performance considerations and heuristics:
- Prioritize hot segments based on profiling: embedding layers and first N transformer blocks are often latency-critical. Provide a per-model default hot list but allow override per-deploy.
- Backpressure for cold downloads: if downloads lag and memory pressure high, pause background fetch until GC frees memory.
- Kernel hints: expose env flags for MAP_POPULATE vs madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) depending on distro.

Compatibility with safetensors / fallback stack:
- Prefer safetensors segments where available; metadata includes tensor-level offsets to allow partial reads. If safetensors absent, support legacy format with adapter that reconstructs a safetensors-like index file stored alongside.
- For safetensors we store per-tensor sha256 and allow lazy materialization of individual tensors for extremely large shards.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a signed manifest (KMS/HSM) for production snapshots? (security team ask)
- How to encode kernel-specific pinning in manifest so that we select the right optimized CUDA/AVX kernel binary? (PR for kernel selection exists but needs manifest hooks)
- GC semantics across dedicated pools (shared storage vs local SSD) need clearer SLOs.

Next steps / action items:
- (Ethan) Prototype atomic symlink swap + token flow in runtime (RUNTIME-742).
- (Ravi) Add generation bitmap invalidation prototype for KV cache; measure invalidation latency.
- (Maya) Draft operator-runbook for canary + rollback and add to Console rollout UI as recommended defaults.

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally informal: it's a collection of heuristics, constraints, and a proposed flow. Feedback welcome on edge cases (esp. mmap semantics on older kernels) and if we should tighten activation_mode semantics into smaller set of supported invariants.

References and links:
- design notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 (proto for activation token)
- jira: RUNTIME-731 (kv generation design), RUNTIME-742 (atomic activation work)
